Problem: Given that $33^{-1} \equiv 77 \pmod{508}$, find $11^{-1} \pmod{508}$ as a residue modulo 508.  (Give an answer between 0 and 507, inclusive.)

message.content:
Since \(33 = 3 \cdot 11\), and we are given

\[
33^{-1} \equiv 77 \pmod{508},
\]

we have

\[
33 \cdot 77 \equiv 1 \pmod{508}.
\]

Substitute \(33 = 3 \cdot 11\):

\[
(3 \cdot 11) \cdot 77 \equiv 1 \pmod{508}.
\]

Rearrange:

\[
11 \cdot (3 \cdot 77) \equiv 1 \pmod{508}.
\]

So the inverse of \(11\) modulo \(508\) is

\[
3 \cdot 77 = 231.
\]

Thus,

\[
11^{-1} \equiv 231 \pmod{508}.
\]

The answer is [231].
